claims.text: The GPS trace for this trip measures 92.0 km between the recorded pickup event and the recorded dropoff event, against a platform optimal route of 22.0 km, so the excess is 70.0 km and 318.2% of optimal. Under POL-RD-01 both establishment tests pass by an enormous margin (excess greater than 20% of optimal, excess greater than 0.8 km) and the excess is additionally MATERIAL (greater than 50% and greater than 8.0 km absolute). The deviation is established on this trip's own trace and materiality is assessed on the excess remaining after any adjustment, of which there is none.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and discharges it: (a) the artifacts describe the same trip, with trip identifier TRP-02835 on the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown, and a common pickup/start timestamp of 2026-09-19T07:00:11+08:00; and (b) the excess meets the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from a trace that is not impaired. No single extra artifact beyond the trace is required here, because the rider's profile does not engage the additional-corroboration condition (see the profile claim below).

The trace is COMPLETE and is NOT impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 834 fixes at a 10.0 second sample interval across 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so none of limbs (a) to (c) (a gap over 90 seconds, a jump over 500 m, a sustained sampling interval over 30 seconds) fires. The deviation therefore stands on the trace alone and needs no independent corroboration; equally, no down-weighting under POL-GEN-02 is available to the driver.

The driver's answer on file - 'The rider was unresponsive and gave no destination' - does not discharge the driver's burden under POL-RD-08 and does not excuse a single kilometre. It invokes none of POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 or POL-RD-12, it points to no artifact and no clause, and POL-RD-08 provides that a general assertion unsupported by a cited artifact carries no weight and is discarded. The trip_record in any event records a platform-registered dropoff point (Blk 36 Marine Cres), so the assertion that no destination existed is contradicted by the record.

No traffic cause can reduce the measured excess. There is no traffic_advisory covering this corridor or window in the bundle: the only advisory artifact is MISSING, carries weight 0.0, and records 'No advisory covers the Blk 12 Telok Blangah Cres corridor in this window'. Under POL-RD-13 the driver's implicit external-cause assertion is tested against the traffic_advisory and nothing else; with no advisory on file POL-RD-03 is unavailable, the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08, and the deviation stands at the full measured figure against the booked optimal route. The absence is citable precisely because the identifier was minted for that purpose.

No rider-requested detour can reduce the excess either. The chat log for this trip is empty - 0 messages, no first or last message timestamp, first_message_at null - so there is no rider instruction meeting POL-RD-04(a) to (c), no waypoint_hint to compare against the 200 m test, and no named road. POL-RD-04 is simply unavailable on this record and no distance is excluded; the excess is decided on the trace as measured.

No relocation and no billing shortfall stands in the driver's favour. The trip_record shows original_pickup, original_dropoff, amended_optimal_distance_km, amended_optimal_duration_min, pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at all null, so there is no amended endpoint and POL-RD-05 cannot be run; and the trip is METERED with distance_charged_km of 92.0 equal to the trace distance, so there is no unbilled-kilometre shortfall of the kind (and the only kind) that would support DRIVER_COMPENSATION under POL-RD-04.

With the deviation established and no exculpatory clause applying, the refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02 and not discretionary. Charged total: 224.12. Recomputed fare: ((3.80 + 0.75 x 22.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x the surge_multiplier recorded on the fare_breakdown, which is 2.0, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and not from the trip_record) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = (3.80 + 16.50 + 8.40) x 2.0 + 0.80 = 58.20. Refund: 224.12 - 58.20 = 165.92, rounded up to 165.95. That is 74.03% of the charged total, below the 90% full-refund share, so the correct outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 165.95, with intermediate values unrounded.

The rider's claim is supported by this trip's own evidence and not by profile. For completeness and to close the point: the repeat-deviation pattern test under POL-RD-06 does NOT fire - driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0, which is below the 3-or-more arm, and 0 divided by completed_trips_90d of 300 is 0.00, which is below the 0.05 arm - so no FINDING against the driver rests on profile, no full refund uplift arises, and no driver-conduct referral is sought. The material deviation was established on the trace alone under POL-RD-01, exactly as POL-RD-06 and POL-GEN-01 require.

No additional corroboration beyond the gps_trace can be demanded of this rider. The POL-RD-08 rider-profile condition requires deviation_claims_60d of 4 or more together with deviation_claims_60d_substantiated of 1 or fewer; the rider's figures are 0 and 0, so the condition is not met, no corroboration requirement attaches, and this factor may never be used to deny a claim that is otherwise proven. The rider's clean claim history supports taking the trace at face value.

The refund is almost entirely a distance-and-time correction; nothing is added on top of it in the pass-through lines. The fare_breakdown carries zero ERP gantries, tolls_erp 0.00 and airport_surcharge 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, so there is no off-route pass-through to refund separately and none to double count. Under POL-RD-09(1) any off-route ERP would already be comprehended in the POL-RD-02 figure and could never be added to it; here the line is zero, so the rider's whole recovery is the 165.95 above.

The result the rider seeks is that he stops carrying a charge for 70 km he never travelled. The POL-RD-02 refund of 165.95 exceeds SGD 150.00, so POL-RD-10(6) means the amount would be held rather than collected at first instance. That is not an obstacle to this claim: held is still money the rider keeps out of the driver's pocket, and on this record no further evidence (no chat instruction, no advisory, no amended optimal, no independent distance figure) could reduce a 318% excess. The rider's position is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 165.95 under POL-RD-02; an escalation under POL-RD-10(6) leaves the disputed amount held, which is likewise a rider win against the present CHARGED state.

claims.text: The deviation is established on this trip's own trace, and the driver does not contest it: under POL-RD-01 the governing field is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, 92.0 km, measured against the booked optimal of 22.0 km, an excess of 70.0 km and 318.2% — MATERIAL on both limbs because it exceeds 50% of optimal and 8.0 km in absolute terms. The trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0: 834 fixes at 10-second sampling, 100.0% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0.0 seconds. Nothing in POL-RD-07 permits the excess to be re-measured in the driver's favour, so the case must run on the POL-RD-02 arithmetic rather than on any figure either advocate might prefer.

POL-RD-06's repeat-deviation test fails on the driver's own profile, so the rider cannot reach FULL_REFUND through it: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 300, which is below the threshold of 3 and gives a ratio of 0.00 against the required 0.05. No pattern is established, so POL-RD-06(b)'s uplift of a material deviation to FULL_REFUND of charged_total does not apply, and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral is licensed. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags (1) is not deviation_flags_90d and may not be substituted for it.

The rider's recovery is arithmetic under POL-RD-02 and is capped there, not discretionary. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 22.0 optimal km + 0.28 x 30.0 optimal min) x 2.0, the surge multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 on-route ERP + 0 fixed surcharge + 0.00 waiting fee - 0.00 promo discount = 58.20. Refund = 224.12 charged_total - 58.20 = 165.92, payable rounded up to SGD 165.95. That is 74.03% of charged_total, below the 90% full-refund share, so the most the rider can be awarded is a PARTIAL_REFUND; the demand in his claim text for the whole $224.12 fare fails on the clause's own arithmetic.

The POL-RD-02 refund of 165.92 exceeds SGD 150.00, so POL-RD-10(6) fires and the judge must NOT issue a final ruling: the case must be ESCALATED to a human reviewer with the full case summary, both briefs and the admissibility report. Escalation is terminal, replaces the ruling, issues no monetary outcome, and holds the disputed amount rather than refunding it. On this record payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so escalation is the only disposition under which the present payment state is left untouched; every monetary remedy the rider seeks is displaced by it.

No exculpatory clause is available to the driver on this record, and the driver does not press one. The chat log carries 0 messages, so POL-RD-04's rider-instruction test cannot be run and no chat_message.waypoint_hint exists to corroborate any requested waypoint; the driver's counterparty statement — 'the rider was unresponsive and gave no destination' — cites no artifact and therefore discharges nothing under POL-RD-08. EV-ADVIS-02835-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-RD-03 is unavailable. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run. The vehicle is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply. The effect is that the excess stands at the measured 70.0 km and the case rises or falls on the POL-RD-02 arithmetic and the POL-RD-10 ceiling alone.

There is nothing for POL-RD-09 to add, and the rider cannot stack a second refund on top of the POL-RD-02 figure. The fare ledger shows an empty erp_gantries list, tolls_erp of 0.00, airport_surcharge of 0.00 on a trip that does not originate at an airport, and zero ERP lines; no off-route or phantom pass-through charge exists, so no standalone pass-through correction is available and no billing-integrity finding arises under POL-RD-09(4). Under POL-RD-09(1) any such charge would in any event already be comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund and must never be added to it, so the rider's total recovery cannot exceed the single POL-RD-02 amount.

Neither party's profile may decide anything in this case. Under POL-GEN-01 only the fields its named tests use can ground a finding; the driver's lifetime counters (prior_deviation_flags, prior_no_show_flags, prior_disputes_filed, prior_disputes_upheld) and the rider's rating, account_age_days and lifetime_trips are context only, and an adverse finding built on any of them must be discarded. In particular rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, so POL-RD-08's additional-corroboration factor does not arise on either side, and the dispute is decided on this trip's trace and fare ledger rather than on reputation.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: the trip itself is not in dispute, but the amount at stake is above the ceiling at which this tribunal may finally rule, so the case goes to a human reviewer and the money is held.

On the trip, the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02835) measures 92.0 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff, against the platform optimal of 22.0 km on the trip record (EV-TRIP-02835). The excess is 70.0 km, or 318.2% of optimal. Under POL-RD-01 the deviation is established and is additionally MATERIAL. The trace is complete — 834 fixes at 10-second intervals, 100% coverage, zero gaps, max gap 0.0 s — so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07 and it stands on its own.

Nothing excuses the excess. The chat log (EV-CHAT-02835) holds no messages, so POL-RD-04 cannot be run. The traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-02835-01) is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-RD-03 is unavailable. The trip record shows no amended pickup or dropoff (all amendment fields null), so POL-RD-05 cannot be run, and the vehicle is RYDE_X rather than RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply. The driver's statement that the rider was unresponsive and gave no destination cites no artifact and discharges no burden under POL-RD-08; it is also contradicted by the recorded dropoff at Blk 36 Marine Cres.

The refund arithmetic is agreed. On this METERED fare, POL-RD-02 gives recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 22.0 km + 0.28 x 30.0 min) x 2.0 surge, read from fare_breakdown EV-FARE-02835) + 0.80 platform fee = 58.20. Refund = 224.12 charged_total - 58.20 = 165.92, rounded up to 165.95, which is 74.03% of the charged total and below the 90% full-refund share. I accept the rider's arithmetic and the driver's arithmetic, which are the same.

That brings the case to POL-RD-10(6). The POL-RD-02 refund of 165.92 exceeds SGD 150.00, and the clause is mandatory: no final ruling may issue and the case must be escalated. Escalation is terminal — it replaces the ruling, no amount is refunded or collected, and the disputed amount is held (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). I therefore reject the rider's submission that a PARTIAL_REFUND of 165.95 should issue notwithstanding limb (6): limb (6) replaces the money outcome rather than sitting beside it. What would resolve the matter is the human reviewer's decision under POL-GEN-06 on the options the money block enumerates; no further evidence in this bundle changes the arithmetic, which rests on artifacts all at weight 1.0.

ruling.explanation:
Trip TRP-02835. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02835, weight 1.0) records 92.0 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a booked optimal of 22.0 km (EV-TRIP-02835), an excess of 70.0 km and 318.2% — a deviation established and material under POL-RD-01 on both limbs, and the trace is complete (834 fixes, 10-second sampling, 100.0% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0.0 s), so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07 and needs no independent corroboration.

No exculpatory clause applies to the driver. The chat log is empty (EV-CHAT-02835, 0 messages), so POL-RD-04's rider-instruction test cannot be run and no waypoint exists to corroborate; EV-ADVIS-02835-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-RD-03 is unavailable; no pickup or dropoff was amended, so POL-RD-05 cannot run; and the vehicle is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply. The driver's statement that the rider gave no destination cites no artifact, discharges nothing under POL-RD-08, and is contradicted by the recorded dropoff at Blk 36 Marine Cres.

The arithmetic under POL-RD-02 is undisputed on both sides. Charged total: 224.12 (EV-FARE-02835). Recomputed fare: ((3.80 + 0.75 x 22.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x 2.0, the surge multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = 58.20. Refund: 224.12 - 58.20 = 165.92, rounded up to 165.95, which is 74.03% of the charge and therefore a partial, not a full, refund. POL-RD-09 adds nothing: there are no ERP gantries, no tolls and no airport surcharge, so no standalone pass-through correction and no billing-integrity finding arises.

I cannot, however, issue that refund as a final ruling. POL-RD-10(6) requires escalation whenever the refund computed under POL-RD-02 exceeds SGD 150.00, and 165.92 does. This is mandatory, and the rider's argument that escalation is 'not an obstacle' because the amount would be held does not change it: POL-RD-10 makes escalation terminal, replacing the ruling and leaving both money fields null. The trigger that fired is POL-RD-10(6) — a POL-RD-02 refund above the SGD 150.00 ceiling. What resolves it is human confirmation of the computation above and release or variation of the held amount; the refund itself is unopposed arithmetic, and only the threshold queuing rule puts it before a reviewer.

The contested amount is accordingly held, not collected or refunded. The rider's separate traffic-cause claim was discarded at the mechanical stage for citing the impaired advisory without disclosing its issue code; it would in any event have failed, since the missing advisory excuses nothing. The repeat-deviation test under POL-RD-06 does not fire (deviation_flags_90d 0 against 300 completed trips, below both arms), so no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises, and neither profile's context-only fields have been used to decide anything.

To both parties — this is what I found and what happens next. The deviation is established on this trip's own evidence. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02835) is complete and unimpaired for policy purposes: 834 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps, no jump over 500 m, so none of POL-RD-07(a)–(c) fires and it governs under POL-RD-01. It records 92.0 km driven against a booked optimal route of 22.0 km — an excess of 70.0 km, or 318.2% of optimal, material on both limbs of POL-RD-01. Nothing excuses it. The chat log (EV-CHAT-02835) is empty (0 messages), so there is no rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04 and no waypoint_hint to corroborate. Pickup and dropoff were never amended and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 cannot run. The only traffic advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-02835-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-RD-03 is unavailable and the driver's implied traffic excuse carries no weight under POL-RD-08. The vehicle is RYDE_X, not a pooled itinerary, so POL-RD-12 does not apply. The driver's statement that the rider was unresponsive and gave no destination cites no artifact and does not discharge the driver's burden under POL-RD-08; the trip record in any event registers a drop-off point. The driver's repeat-deviation test also fails on his own profile (deviation_flags_90d 0 against 300 completed trips), so no POL-RD-06(b) full-refund uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises. The fare ledger carries no ERP gantries, no tolls and no airport surcharge, so POL-RD-09 adds nothing. The POL-RD-02 arithmetic is therefore: charged total 224.12; recomputed fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 × 22.0 km + 0.28 × 30.0 min) × 2.0 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee = 58.20; refund = 224.12 − 58.20 = 165.92, rounded up to 165.95, which is 74.03% of the charge and below the 90% full-refund share. The rider's submission that the correct outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND of 165.95 states the arithmetic correctly but does not dispose of the case: that refund exceeds SGD 150.00, and POL-RD-10(6) makes it a mandatory escalation. So the ruling is ESCALATE. Escalation is terminal — it replaces any money ruling, so no amount is refunded and no amount is collected, and the disputed 224.12 is held rather than collected or refunded. A human reviewer will confirm the computation set out above and release the amount; no further evidence could change it, since there is no chat instruction, no advisory and no amended optimal on the record. This threshold is not a finding against either party, and the outcome is provisional without human review.

To both parties. The deviation on this trip is not in dispute. The GPS trace EV-GPS-02835 records 92.0 km between the pickup and drop-off events; the platform optimal on EV-TRIP-02835 is 22.0 km. That is an excess of 70.0 km, or 318.2% of optimal, far past both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (>20% and >0.8 km) and a MATERIAL deviation on both limbs (>50% and >8.0 km). The trace is complete (834 fixes, 10-second sampling, 100.0% coverage, no gaps) and is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c), so it decides the measurement on its own and needs no corroboration. Neither side contests this, and both advocates compute the same excess.

Nothing excuses the excess. The chat log EV-CHAT-02835 is empty (0 messages), so POL-RD-04 cannot be run and no rider-requested distance is excluded. No endpoint was amended (amended_optimal_distance_km and both amendment timestamps are null), so POL-RD-05 cannot be run. On POL-RD-06 the driver's trailing-90-day deviation flags are 0 against 300 completed trips, so no repeat pattern is established: there is no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral. To the human reviewer: the arithmetic is not in doubt and no artifact on this record can reduce a 318% excess, so no further evidence is needed to fix the figure. Confidence rests on EV-GPS-02835, EV-TRIP-02835 and EV-FARE-02835, all at weight_multiplier 1.0; no impaired artifact carries a deciding fact, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0.
